# Live Validation — Theology (skill arm)

- **Date:** 2026-08-08
- **Skill:** `find-university-chairs` (current version — delegates discovery to
  `discover-university-candidates`)
- **Run type:** blind (Task V′). Only the `Sample interest:` line of
  `skills/tests/eval_ground_truth/theology.md` was read before this run, via `grep`.

## Persona

- **Interests:** Biblical studies (Old and New Testament exegesis) and the history of
  early Christianity, including the Jewish and Greco-Roman religious context and
  early-church / late-antique church history. *(verbatim from the GT sample-interest line)*
- **Methods:** historical-critical exegesis, philological close reading of primary
  sources, source and redaction criticism, historical contextualisation.
- **Domain:** theology / ancient religious history — Second Temple Judaism, Hellenistic
  religion, early Christianity, late antiquity.
- **Thesis style:** text-based argumentative monograph; close reading of primary texts
  against secondary literature; no empirical data collection.
- **Skills:** Biblical Hebrew, Koine Greek, Latin; German and English academic reading;
  standard exegetical methodology.
- **No-gos:** practical/pastoral theology and homiletics; religious education
  (Religionspädagogik); quantitative/empirical social-science-of-religion work.
  Systematic/dogmatic theology treated as *off-core*, not as a hard no-go.

## Vacancy finding (reported before the option map, deliberately)

The Protestant faculty carries **six vacant (N.N.) chairs** of sixteen. Two of them sit
**directly on this persona's focus** and therefore cannot be offered as thesis options:

| Chair | Designation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Altes Testament I | "Literaturgeschichte des Alten Testaments" | **N.N. — vacant** |
| Neues Testament II | "Evangelienforschung" (Gospel research) | **N.N. — vacant** |
| Kirchenordnung und Neuere Kirchengeschichte | — | N.N. — vacant (off-core anyway) |
| Systematische Theologie II | "Ethik und Christliche Gesellschaftslehre" | N.N. — vacant (off-core) |
| Systematische Theologie III | "Fundamentaltheologie und Religionsphilosophie" | N.N. — vacant (off-core) |
| Praktische Theologie II | "Religionspädagogik" | N.N. — vacant (no-go area anyway) |

Source: <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/>
(verified 2026-08-08), confirmed on the AT and NT department pages.

**Gospel research — the single closest label to "New Testament exegesis" in the whole
faculty — has no chair holder.** No successor or acting cover (Vertretung) is named on
the page. The same is true of the OT literary-history chair. This is a real constraint
on the student, not a discovery gap: do not read the chair designation as an available
supervisor. The Catholic faculty's `Philosophische Grundfragen der Theologie` is also
N.N., which matters only because it is one of the two chairs jointly running the
Augustinus-Zentrum (Drecoll carries the Protestant half).

## Option map — grouped by interest dimension

### A. New Testament exegesis + Jewish / Greco-Roman religious context

**1. Lehrstuhl für Neues Testament I — Institut für antikes Judentum und hellenistische Religionsgeschichte**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Michael Tilly · **Unit type:** chair + institute
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/neues-testament/neues-testament-i/tilly-michael-prof-dr/>
- **Relevance:** the single closest match in the university. Chair explicitly couples NT
  with ancient Judaism and Hellenistic religious history — the persona's "Jewish and
  Greco-Roman religious context" is this chair's constitutive remit. Research: literature
  and religion of ancient Judaism, Septuagint, Tosefta, transmission and interpretation of
  scripture in ancient Judaism *and early Christianity*, early Christian ethics.
- **Pros / difficulties:** exact topical fit and an institute infrastructure. Expect
  Hebrew + Greek to be assumed rather than taught; Septuagint/Tosefta work needs
  philological confidence.
- **Evidence:** chair + institute pages, verified 2026-08-08; monograph record on ancient
  Jewish religious sociology in the Hellenistic-Roman period. **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask how a thesis could use Septuagint transmission evidence to
  trace a specific NT motif back into its Hellenistic-Jewish setting.

**2. Lehrstuhl für Neues Testament III — Paulus und die Paulusschule, Theologie und Hermeneutik des NT**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Christof Landmesser · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/neues-testament/neues-testament-iii/>
- **Relevance:** NT exegesis with a Pauline and hermeneutical focus; currently leads a
  DFG-Forschungsgruppe subproject on "Sakralisierung und Desakralisierung in und von Texten
  des Neuen Testaments" — an active, thesis-sized textual-analysis programme.
- **Pros / difficulties:** clearly active third-party-funded context (chair member awarded
  the Leopold-Lucas early-career prize, May 2026). Hermeneutics-heavy framing may pull a
  thesis toward theory if the student wants pure historical work.
- **Evidence:** chair page, verified 2026-08-08. **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask whether a Pauline-letter thesis could be framed within the
  sacralisation project's categories.

**3. Lehrstuhl für Neues Testament (Katholisch-Theologische Fakultät)**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Wilfried Eisele · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/katholisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle/neues-testament/lehrstuhl/team/prof-dr-wilfried-eisele/>
- **Relevance:** NT exegesis with focus on Luke-Acts and Hebrews; habilitation on the
  **text and transmission history of the Gospel of Thomas**, and co-edited work on
  transmission processes in early Christianity — directly on the persona's
  exegesis + early-Christianity axis. Partly fills the gap left by the vacant
  Evangelienforschung chair on the Protestant side.
- **Pros / difficulties:** in Tübingen since 2017, active. Cross-faculty supervision
  (Protestant student → Catholic faculty) needs checking with the examination office.
- **Evidence:** chair/team page, verified 2026-08-08; *Kurzgefasste Einleitung in das Neue
  Testament* (2021). **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask how apocryphal-gospel transmission evidence bears on
  canonical Gospel exegesis.

### B. Early-church / late-antique church history

**4. Lehrstuhl für Kirchengeschichte II — Schwerpunkt Alte Kirche**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Volker Henning Drecoll · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/kirchengeschichte/kirchengeschichte-ii/drecoll-volker-henning-prof-dr/>
- **Relevance:** the Protestant faculty's early-church chair — patristics and late
  antiquity, exactly the persona's church-history strand. Currently runs a DFG project on
  Basil's Hexaemeron homilies and published *Basil of Caesarea as Exegete* (Tübingen,
  2025); co-directs the **Augustinus-Zentrum** (first critical bilingual German Augustine
  edition), a cross-faculty structure with Catholic theology and philosophy.
- **Pros / difficulties:** patristic exegesis sits on the exegesis/church-history seam the
  persona occupies, so a thesis can face either way. Greek/Latin patristic sources are
  demanding; the Augustine edition is an editorial project, not a thesis pipeline.
- **Evidence:** chair page + 2025 monograph + DFG record, verified 2026-08-08.
  **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask whether a thesis could read one Hexaemeron homily as
  evidence for how a late-antique bishop handled OT exegesis.

**5. Lehrstuhl für Alte Kirchengeschichte, Patrologie und Christliche Archäologie (Kath. Fak.)**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Thomas Jürgasch · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/katholisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle/alte-kirchengeschichte-patrologie-und-christliche-archaeologie/lehrstuhl/>
- **Relevance:** second early-church chair in Tübingen, adding patrology *and* Christian
  archaeology — material as well as textual access to late antiquity. Recent volume with
  A. M. Karimi marking the 1700th anniversary of Nicaea (2025); an international conference
  at the chair is scheduled for 1 October 2026.
- **Pros / difficulties:** W3 appointment confirmed via university personnel news
  (Newsletter 1/2026), so this is a currently-staffed chair. The chair-holder page 404'd
  during this run — use the Lehrstuhl page above. Cross-faculty supervision caveat as in #3.
- **Evidence:** Lehrstuhl + Aktuelles pages and Uni-Tübingen Personalnachrichten 1/2026,
  verified 2026-08-08. **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask how the Nicaea-anniversary work reframes fourth-century
  conciliar sources for a thesis-scale question.

### C. Old Testament exegesis

**6. Lehrstuhl für Altes Testament II — Theologie des Alten Testaments**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Martin Leuenberger · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/altes-testament/>
- **Relevance:** with AT I vacant, this is the Protestant faculty's **only** occupied
  general OT exegesis chair — the default route for the persona's OT strand.
- **Pros / difficulties:** carries the OT teaching load for a department running one chair
  short, so supervision capacity is a fair question to ask early.
- **Evidence:** department page, verified 2026-08-08 (chair-level evidence; no separate
  publication-currency check run this pass — **medium confidence**).
  **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask which OT corpus currently has open thesis-scale questions
  at the chair.

**7. Lehrstuhl für Altes Testament (Katholisch-Theologische Fakultät)**
- **Person:** Prof'in Dr'in Ruth Scoralick · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/katholisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle/altes-testament/lehrstuhl/prof-dr-ruth-scoralick/>
- **Relevance:** OT exegesis, in Tübingen since 2011/12; research focus on biblical wisdom
  literature (Proverbs). A second OT route while AT I is vacant.
- **Pros / difficulties:** wisdom literature is a narrower entry point than the persona's
  broad OT interest; cross-faculty supervision caveat.
- **Evidence:** chair page, verified 2026-08-08. **No-go flags:** none.
- **Conversation starter:** ask how wisdom-literature methods transfer to another OT corpus.

### D. Material and comparative context (flagged — adjacent, not core)

**8. Biblisch-Archäologisches Institut (BAI) / Lehrstuhl für Biblische Archäologie**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Jens Kamlah · **Unit type:** institute + chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/altes-testament/biblisch-archaeologisches-institut/>
- **Relevance:** supplies the material-culture context for the biblical world; active field
  projects (Tell el-Burak, Emar, Beirut) and SFB 1070 "RessourcenKulturen" subproject A06
  on the Late Bronze/Iron Age Levant. Teaching runs through 2025/26 with an excursion in
  May 2026; Kamlah is Vice Dean since 2025.
- **⚠ Flag — method mismatch, kept not dropped:** the persona's method is textual/exegetical,
  not archaeological, and field participation may be expected. Relevant as *context* for a
  text-based thesis rather than as a primary home. Included with this warning per the
  enrich-before-exclude rule.
- **Evidence:** institute, teaching and SFB pages, verified 2026-08-08.
- **Conversation starter:** ask whether a text-led thesis could use BAI material evidence
  without doing fieldwork.

**9. Lehrstuhl für Religionswissenschaft, Schwerpunkt Judaistik**
- **Person:** Prof. Dr. Holger Zellentin · **Unit type:** chair
- **URL:** <https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/evangelisch-theologische-fakultaet/lehrstuehle-und-institute/religionswissenschaft-und-judaistik/religionswissenschaft-und-judaistik/seminar/>
- **Relevance:** late-antique Judaism, Christianity and Islam in contact; work on Jesus'
  confirmation of the Torah across the three traditions and on Palestinian Midrash —
  squarely the persona's Jewish-context and late-antiquity strands.
- **⚠ Flag — centre of gravity has shifted:** the chair's current output is dominated by the
  ERC project **QaSLA ("The Qur'an as a Source for Late Antiquity")** and early-Islamic
  topics (Cambridge Bennett Lecture, March 2026; Qur'anic-studies conferences 2025–26).
  Late-antique Judaism/Christianity remains genuinely in scope, but a thesis here would
  likely sit in a Qur'anic/comparative frame. Kept with the flag rather than dropped.
- **Evidence:** seminar page, verified 2026-08-08.
- **Conversation starter:** ask whether a thesis on a Jewish-Christian late-antique text
  could be supervised outside the QaSLA frame.

## Excluded (recorded, not silently dropped)

- **Kirchengeschichte I / Witt** (Reformation and Middle Ages) and **Mittlere und Neuere
  Kirchengeschichte / Holzem** (Kath.) — church history, but the wrong period; the persona
  specifies early-church/late-antique.
- **Systematische Theologie I / Linde**, **Fundamentaltheologie / Wendel**, **Dogmatik /
  Rahner, Pittl**, **Moraltheologie / Bormann**, **Theologische Ethik / Möhring-Hesse**,
  **Kirchenrecht / Anuth**, **Liturgiewissenschaft / Winter** — off-core systematic,
  ethical and legal fields; no exegetical or early-church remit.
- **Praktische Theologie I / Kretzschmar**, **III / Weyel**, **Praktische Theologie /
  Schüßler**, **Religionspädagogik / Boschki** — confirmed no-go match.
- **Biblische Sprachen / Dr. Hepperle** (Kath.) — language instruction post, not a research
  chair; excluded as non-supervising, not as irrelevant.
